learning_outcomes.text: Understand and evaluate the process of generation, transport, distribution and storage of electrical energy, with special emphasis on generation and storage processes for remote applications.
Analyze and size the protection systems of a simple low voltage installation.

Understand the specific characteristics that distinguish power diodes and MOSFET transistors from signal ones and understand the operation of other electronic devices used exclusively in power applications (IGBTs, SCRs, Triacs and GTOs).
Understand the operation of uncontrolled single-phase and three-phase rectifiers and calculate the voltages and currents in their components.
Analyze, quantify and design linear power supplies.
Understand the operation of basic DC/DC converters and single-phase DC/AC converters and calculate the voltages and currents in their components.
Analyze the operation of simple power electronic systems of special interest in the world of telecommunications.
Perform simulation of general-purpose electronic circuits with computer tools.
Select semiconductor devices and power capacitors for a known application.
Calculate power magnetic components (coils and transformers) for a known application.
Understand the operation of controlled and semi-controlled single-phase and three-phase rectifiers and calculate the voltages and currents in their components.

syllabus_topics: Principles of switched DC-DC conversion: Pulse width modulators
Electronic devices for power electronic converters
Examples of power electronic systems for telecommunications

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory practices (tasks and final practical exam)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as 20% for Laboratory Practices (PL) and 80% for the Theoretical part. The Theoretical part is weighted as 18%·B1 + 12%·B2 + 20%·B3.A + 50% B3.B. A minimum score of 3 out of 10 is required for each evaluable component (PL, B1, B2, B3.A, B3.B). If minimums are not reached, the course is failed, and the final grade will be the minimum between 4 and the weighted score. For the extraordinary call, the PL grade is conserved, and the theoretical part is reevaluated if minimums were not met.
